labels.label: ersthm:ThmNonUniqueness
labels.serves: Most directly. The row's 'causally: two flat 1+1 developments with overlapping developing maps' is, in its topological half, not_injective_and_not_descends. A point x ∈ U_a ∩ U_b with Φ_a(x) ≠ Φ_b(x) (the conclusion) lies outside every A on which the two agree. So π is not injective at x, and the Einstein-style solution ũ lives on no subset of the background (exists_glue_eq_comp_proj_iff). With A the component through S, E is still Hausdorff (t2Space_connectedComponentIn) and second countable (secondCountableTopology).
labels.remains: The theorem itself: the existence of the two Born–Infeld GHDs (layer 3, T-loc-born-infeld-causal), and the causal half of T-abs-ers-etale-mghd: that the gluing along the MCGHD is a GHD over the background, i.e. the lifted S is a Cauchy surface of E for the glued causality.

labels.label: ersthm:global_theorem
labels.serves: Only the last topological step. An injective étale map is an open embedding, and the gluing is then U₁ ∪ U₂ (isOpenEmbedding_proj, exists_homeomorph). Thm 3.35's content, that Ψ is injective when Φ₁'²Φ₂'² < 1, is the monotonicity of F(·; η) (layer 3).
labels.remains: Everything of the row: Ψ is the developing map of one development, not the projection of a two-piece gluing. The row stays layer 3.

labels.label: erslem:sep_lemma
labels.serves: The target that the separation lemma decides, in the two-piece case: π fails to be injective exactly over U₁ ∩ U₂ ∖ A, with two points over each such x (injective_proj_iff, encard_preimage_proj_singleton_of_notMem). Lemma 3.32's spacelike/timelike separation of the two preimages is causal and layer 3.
labels.remains: The separation of preimages itself (T-loc-born-infeld-causal, T-loc-quasilinear-nesting), and the causal half's use of it: two preimages of one point cannot both lie in one GH development in the superluminal case.

labels.label: ersthm:diffeo_theorem
labels.serves: Nothing directly. Thm 3.22 is a cited PDE fact (the hodograph). The étale vocabulary here (a local homeomorphism to the background whose non-injectivity is the obstruction) is the one the row's note uses for Ψ.

labels.label: erslem:nec_cond
labels.serves: Nothing directly. Lemma 3.23 says where Ψ is a local homeomorphism (the Jacobian), a layer-3 computation. Here π is a local homeomorphism everywhere by construction.

labels.label: erslem:lemma_sing

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing

declarations.role: (4) the glued function ũ := Gluing.desc (u₁ ∘ coe) (u₂ ∘ coe) of two functions agreeing on A

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.eq_of_proj_eq
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} {z z' : Causal.EtaleGluing h₁ h₂}, Causal.EtaleGluing.proj h₁ h₂ z = Causal.EtaleGluing.proj h₁ h₂ z' → (Causal.EtaleGluing.proj h₁ h₂ z ∈ U₁ ∩ U₂ → Causal.EtaleGluing.proj h₁ h₂ z ∈ A) → z = z'
declarations.role: helper: two points over one point x are equal when x ∈ U₁ ∩ U₂ forces x ∈ A

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.injective_proj_iff

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.ι₁_ne_ι₂
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} {x : M} (hx₁ : x ∈ U₁) (hx₂ : x ∈ U₂), x ∉ A → Causal.Gluing.ι₁ (Set.inclusion h₁) (Set.inclusion h₂) ⟨x, hx₁⟩ ≠ Causal.Gluing.ι₂ (Set.inclusion h₁) (Set.inclusion h₂) ⟨x, hx₂⟩
declarations.role: (2) over x ∈ U₁ ∩ U₂ ∖ A the two sheets do not meet

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.preimage_proj_singleton_of_mem_inter
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} {x : M} (hx₁ : x ∈ U₁) (hx₂ : x ∈ U₂), Causal.EtaleGluing.proj h₁ h₂ ⁻¹' {x} = {Causal.Gluing.ι₁ (Set.inclusion h₁) (Set.inclusion h₂) ⟨x, hx₁⟩, Causal.Gluing.ι₂ (Set.inclusion h₁) (Set.inclusion h₂) ⟨x, hx₂⟩}
declarations.role: (2) over x ∈ U₁ ∩ U₂ the fibre is {ι₁ x, ι₂ x} (stronger than the target: no x ∉ A needed for the set equality)

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.encard_preimage_proj_singleton_of_notMem
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} {x : M}, x ∈ U₁ → x ∈ U₂ → x ∉ A → (Causal.EtaleGluing.proj h₁ h₂ ⁻¹' {x}).encard = 2
declarations.role: (2) the fibre over x ∈ U₁ ∩ U₂ ∖ A has exactly two points

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.preimage_proj_singleton_of_mem
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} {x : M}, x ∈ U₁ ∪ U₂ → x ∉ (U₁ ∩ U₂) \ A → ∃ z, Causal.EtaleGluing.proj h₁ h₂ ⁻¹' {x} = {z}

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.preimage_proj_singleton_of_notMem_union
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} {x : M}, x ∉ U₁ ∪ U₂ → Causal.EtaleGluing.proj h₁ h₂ ⁻¹' {x} = ∅
declarations.role: (2) off U₁ ∪ U₂ the fibre is empty

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.preimage_proj_eq_union

declarations.role: (2) π⁻¹(B) is the union of its two sheets ι₁(B ∩ U₁), ι₂(B ∩ U₂), for any B

declarations.role: (2) 'contains the other components twice' (:852): for B disjoint from A the two sheets are disjoint

declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} [inst : TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M], IsOpen A → ∀ {x : ↑U₁} {y : ↑U₂}, Causal.Gluing.IsCorrespondingBoundaryPair (Set.inclusion h₁) (Set.inclusion h₂) x y ↔ ↑x = ↑y ∧ ↑x ∈ closure A \ A

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.glue_ι₁
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} {β : Type u_2} {u₁ u₂ : M → β} {hu : Set.EqOn u₁ u₂ A} (x : ↑U₁), Causal.EtaleGluing.glue h₁ h₂ u₁ u₂ hu (Causal.Gluing.ι₁ (Set.inclusion h₁) (Set.inclusion h₂) x) = u₁ ↑x

declarations.name: Causal.EtaleGluing.glue_ι₂
declarations.statement: ∀ {M : Type u_1} {U₁ U₂ A : Set M} {h₁ : A ⊆ U₁} {h₂ : A ⊆ U₂} {β : Type u_2} {u₁ u₂ : M → β} {hu : Set.EqOn u₁ u₂ A} (y : ↑U₂), Causal.EtaleGluing.glue h₁ h₂ u₁ u₂ hu (Causal.Gluing.ι₂ (Set.inclusion h₁) (Set.inclusion h₂) y) = u₂ ↑y

binder_proposal.note_append: The topological half of T-abs-ers-etale-mghd is T-abs-ers-etale-gluing (Causal.EtaleGluing). Gluing U_a, U_b along an open A on which Φ_a = Φ_b gives E with π : E → U_a ∪ U_b étale (isLocalHomeomorph_proj). π is injective iff U_a ∩ U_b ⊆ A (injective_proj_iff). E is Hausdorff iff A is closed in U_a ∩ U_b (t2Space_iff), so E is Hausdorff when A is a component (t2Space_connectedComponentIn). Thm 3.45's conclusion is exactly the failure of the glued solution to descend to the background (exists_glue_eq_comp_proj_iff, not_injective_and_not_descends). The causal half (lifted S a Cauchy surface of E) stays with T-abs-ers-etale-mghd.

binder_proposal.note_append: On the Einstein-style gluing (T-abs-ers-etale-gluing): Causal.EtaleGluing.not_isPreconnected_inter is the corollary's shape with 'the gluing along the MCGHD is Hausdorff' as its input, for any space: disagreement at a point of U₁ ∩ U₂ and a Hausdorff gluing along a non-empty open A force U₁ ∩ U₂ to be disconnected. Its topological core is eq_inter_of_t2Space (a Hausdorff gluing over a connected overlap has A = U₁ ∩ U₂).

findings: Paper, precision rather than error (ghd_02_19.tex:852). 'glueing them together along the MCGHD ... would yield a solution which is no longer defined on a subset of ℝ^{d+1}' runs together two failures. (i) The space E is not a subset of the background as soon as U₁ ∩ U₂ ⊄ A (injective_proj_iff). With A the MCGHD, which lies in the component of U₁ ∩ U₂ through S (:850), this happens whenever U₁ ∩ U₂ is disconnected, whatever u₁ and u₂ are. (ii) The glued solution ũ fails to live on a subset of the background exactly when u₁ ≠ u₂ somewhere on U₁ ∩ U₂ (exists_glue_eq_comp_proj_iff). (i) can hold without (ii): punctured_witness, last conjunct (U₁ = U₂ = ℝ ∖ {0}, A = (0, ∞) a component, u₁ = u₂ = 0; π is not injective and ũ = 0 ∘ π). In that case ũ descends to U₁ ∪ U₂ and nothing is 'not allowed'. ERS's conclusion (:852: 'the key difference ... the underlying manifold is constructed along with the solution') concerns (ii). Its link to disconnectedness is Cor 4.68 (:921), whose topological shape is not_isPreconnected_inter.

Programme statement, not the paper. T-abs-ers-etale-mghd's title says the Einstein-style gluing along the MCGHD carries a local homeomorphism to the background 'injective iff they agree on the whole overlap'. Read on the projection π, this is false as topology. With A the MCGHD, π is injective iff U₁ ∩ U₂ ⊆ A. Given :850 (the MCGHD is the component of U₁ ∩ U₂ through S), that holds iff U₁ ∩ U₂ is connected. Agreement on the whole overlap is the descent of ũ (exists_glue_eq_comp_proj_iff). The topological counterexample to 'agree ⇒ injective' is punctured_witness's last conjunct. The causal half should state the two separately: π injective ⇔ U₁ ∩ U₂ = MCGHD (connected overlap, Sbierski's tacit assumption, :850); ũ descends ⇔ u₁ = u₂ on U₁ ∩ U₂. Only the second is fixed-background uniqueness. The candidate-3 sentence of references/sbierski/notes/eperon2018predictability.md (:67, 'uniqueness of the MGHD in the fixed-background sense ⇔ this map is injective') needs the same care if it is read for two developments.

Paper, confirmed (ghd_02_19.tex:852, 'a manifold which projects down on U₁ ∪ U₂ ... and contains the other connected components of U₁ ∩ U₂ twice'). Its topology is proved: π is a surjective local homeomorphism onto U₁ ∪ U₂ (isLocalHomeomorph_codRestrict_proj). Over each point of U₁ ∩ U₂ ∖ A there are exactly two points (encard_preimage_proj_singleton_of_notMem), and over a set disjoint from A two disjoint sheets (preimage_proj_eq_union, disjoint_image_ι₁_image_ι₂). E is Hausdorff when A is a component in a locally connected Hausdorff background (t2Space_connectedComponentIn), and second countable (secondCountableTopology). The Hausdorff property needs A to be the whole component: gluing along a smaller open set with a frontier point in U₁ ∩ U₂ gives a non-Hausdorff E (t2Space_iff, branching_witness). So ':850' is load-bearing for 'a manifold', which ERS do not say.
questions: Reading of 'a manifold which projects down on U₁ ∪ U₂' (:852). Taken: π is a local homeomorphism with range U₁ ∪ U₂ (and its corestriction a surjective local homeomorphism), and E is Hausdorff and second countable. The smooth structure (charts pulled back along π) and 'a solution' on E (the PDE) are not formalized, being layer 3. If the author wants E as a smooth manifold, that needs a smooth-manifold layer the package does not have.

Reading of 'contains the other connected components of U₁ ∩ U₂ twice' (:852). Taken: every point of U₁ ∩ U₂ ∖ A has exactly two preimages, and over any B disjoint from A the preimage is the disjoint union of the two sheets ι₁(B), ι₂(B), each mapped onto B by π (an open embedding on each sheet). It is not stated per connected component, which needs nothing more.

Reading of 'glueing along the MCGHD'. Taken: A is any open subset of U₁ ∩ U₂ with u₁ = u₂ on A. That the MCGHD is the component of U₁ ∩ U₂ through S (:850, the argument of Thm 4.64) is causal and left to T-abs-ers-etale-mghd. The component case is t2Space_connectedComponentIn, and the connected case is eq_inter_of_t2Space.
kb_proposals: Two subsets U₁, U₂ of one space glued along A ⊆ U₁ ∩ U₂: Causal.EtaleGluing h₁ h₂ (Gluing of the two Set.inclusion maps), π = EtaleGluing.proj. π is injective iff U₁ ∩ U₂ ⊆ A (no topology). π is étale for U₁, U₂, A open. E is Hausdorff iff U₁ ∩ U₂ ∩ closure A ⊆ A when M is T2 (t2Space_iff); the forward direction holds for any M (subset_of_t2Space). Glued functions descend iff they agree on U₁ ∩ U₂ (CausalScaffold.ErsEtaleGluing, T-abs-ers-etale-gluing).

Pattern: a map out of a Causal.Gluing is a local homeomorphism when its composite with each ι_i is. Take IsLocalHomeomorphOn.of_comp_right on each sheet (f := ι_i, an open embedding; g ∘ f a local homeomorphism), then cover by Gluing.exists_ι (Causal.EtaleGluing.isLocalHomeomorph_proj).

Pitfall: injectivity of the Einstein-style projection measures the connectedness of U₁ ∩ U₂ (A a component), not the agreement of the two solutions; agreement is descent (Causal.EtaleGluing.exists_glue_eq_comp_proj_iff). The two come apart at punctured_witness.

Names at this pin: secondCountableTopology_of_countable_cover is TopologicalSpace.secondCountableTopology_of_countable_cover (not exported by `open Topology`); isClosed_preimage_val : IsClosed (s ↓∩ t) ↔ s ∩ closure (s ∩ t) ⊆ t is the one-line route from 'closed in s' to a closure inclusion; IsPreconnected.subset_of_closure_inter_subset proves a connected set lies in a relatively clopen open set.
what_remains: Nothing of the target: all five deliverables are proved with no sorry, plus the planner's optional glueSolutions form, checked by rfl in the probe. What remains is T-abs-ers-etale-mghd's causal half. (a) The glued causality on E: Causal.Gluing.causality with CompatibleAlong on A, supplied by CausalityFollows where u₁ = u₂. (b) That the lifted S is a Cauchy surface of E, so that E is a development over the background in the étale sense: through ETT's prop:ppcm_Cauchy (Causal.CBG.ett_ppcm_Cauchy, waiting on T-abs-hoist-cbg-geometry, OQ-97), or directly, since an inextensible curve of E crosses between the sheets only through ι(A). (c) That the MCGHD is the component of U₁ ∩ U₂ through S (:850, Thm 4.64), which with t2Space_connectedComponentIn makes E Hausdorff. (d) Lemma 3.32's separation of preimages (layer 3). It should also restate its title per the second finding: π injective ⇔ connected overlap; descent ⇔ agreement.

corrected_after_audit: AUDIT-1 (minor), recorded by the master: finding (2) is read with two precisions. (a) The title's forward direction holds: π injective implies u₁ = u₂ on U₁ ∩ U₂ (from injective_proj_iff and agreement on A; checked by the auditor in Lean). (b) The counterexample to 'agreement ⇒ injective' (punctured_witness) is topological only: its A is a component chosen by hand, not the MCGHD of two GHDs; whether two GHDs can agree on all of a disconnected overlap is a causal/PDE question this module does not decide. Restated: π injective ⇔ U₁ ∩ U₂ ⊆ A (given :850, the overlap connected); the glued function descends ⇔ u₁ = u₂ on the overlap; 'agreement ⇒ injective' stays an open causal question for T-abs-ers-etale-mghd. Finding (3): ERS state at :852's parenthetical that the MCGHD is the component; what they do not say is that the glued space's Hausdorff property rests on it.
